note: Borders: historical-basemaps by André Ourednik (GitHub aourednik/historical-basemaps, commit da7a4b7 of 15 Sep 2026, GPL-3.0). The project marks every border as approximate (BORDERPRECISION 1) and asks users to check it against other sources. Orbis clipped the maps to the regions its stories show, simplified them and grouped the polygons into states (drawn with borders) and peoples, cultures and nomadic groups (drawn as soft areas: their extent is an estimate). Maps used: 2000 BC (Anatolia and its neighbours only), 200 BC, 100 BC, AD 1, 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500. Each is shown from its year until the next, except: 200 BC until 146 BC (Carthage destroyed); 100 BC until 58 BC (Caesar's Gallic War); AD 1 from 30 BC (Egypt annexed) to AD 43 (Britain invaded); AD 100 from AD 43 to 106 (Dacia conquered; this map still has Dacia independent); AD 200 from 106 to 293; AD 300 from 293 (its four Tetrarchy shares until 324, then merged as one empire until 395); AD 400 from 395 to 476; AD 500 from 476. In the gaps (300-146 BC, 146-100 BC, 58-30 BC) no map is shown: the century maps would draw Rome's extent wrongly there. Corrections: the AD 300 map's 'Parthian Empire' is labelled Sasanian (from 224); the AD 500 map's 'Western Roman Empire' is the Domain of Soissons. Most 2000 BC areas are peoples and culture zones, not states. This derived file is distributed under the GNU GPL v3, like its source.
